analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־

draft.change: Add Genesis 15:7 as an example of the existing sense to-a-person-speaking for אֶל.
draft.definition: With a verb of speaking, אֶל marks the person addressed.
draft.evidence: In Genesis 15:7, וַיֹּאמֶר אֵלָיו introduces Yahweh’s words to Abram. The third-person suffix names the addressee from the narrator’s perspective, and Yahweh addresses him in the second person in הוֹצֵאתִיךָ.

analysis.evidence: וַיֹּאמֶר אֵלָיו means “he said to him.” The speaker identifies himself as Yahweh in אֲנִי יַהְוֶה and addresses Abram directly in הוֹצֵאתִיךָ, “I brought you out.”
analysis.morphology: The preposition אֶל takes a third-person masculine singular pronominal suffix referring to Abram.

analysis.evidence: In אֲנִי יַהְוֶה, “I am Yahweh,” the pronoun is the subject and the divine name identifies the speaker. The following אֲשֶׁר הוֹצֵאתִיךָ, “who brought you out,” identifies him further by his action.
analysis.morphology: Independent first-person common singular personal pronoun, with no prefix or suffix.
Proper noun, masculine singular, without prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: Personal name of the God of Israel

analysis.evidence: אֲשֶׁר introduces a relative clause describing יַהְוֶה. In אֲנִי יַהְוֶה אֲשֶׁר הוֹצֵאתִיךָ, “I am Yahweh, who brought you out,” the first-person verb identifies Yahweh as the speaker who brought Abram out.
analysis.morphology: Uninflected Hebrew relative particle with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: אֲנִי יַהְוֶה identifies YHWH as the speaker. The suffix ךָ refers to Abram, and מֵאוּר כַּשְׂדִּים names Ur of the Chaldeans as the place from which YHWH brought him out.
analysis.morphology: Hiphil perfect, first person common singular, with a second person masculine singular object suffix.

analysis.evidence: After הוֹצֵאתִיךָ (“I brought you out”), מֵאוּר names the place of departure. The following כַּשְׂדִּים identifies it as Ur of the Chaldeans.
analysis.morphology: The prefixed preposition מִן takes the form מֵ before א. It governs the proper noun אוּר.

draft.change: Add Genesis 15:7 as an example of the existing ethnic sense.
draft.definition: A member of the Chaldean people. The plural can name the people collectively.
draft.evidence: Genesis 15:7 repeats the designation מֵאוּר כַּשְׂדִּים from Genesis 11:31.

analysis.evidence: In הוֹצֵאתִיךָ מֵאוּר כַּשְׂדִּים, “I brought you out of Ur of the Chaldeans,” כַּשְׂדִּים identifies Ur by the people associated with it. Genesis 11:31 uses the same phrase for Abram’s departure.
analysis.morphology: Masculine plural absolute of the gentilic noun כַּשְׂדִּי, used as a people’s name. It completes the construct phrase אוּר כַּשְׂדִּים and has no prefix or pronominal suffix.
analysis.sense: a member of the Chaldean people

analysis.evidence: לְךָ identifies Abram as the recipient, אֶת הָאָרֶץ הַזֹּאת identifies “this land” as the gift, and לְרִשְׁתָּהּ specifies that Abram is to possess it.
analysis.morphology: The preposition לָ־ introduces the Qal infinitive construct תֶת and expresses the purpose of הוֹצֵאתִיךָ (“I brought you out”).
analysis.sense: give land to someone as a possession

analysis.evidence: In לָתֶת לְךָ אֶת הָאָרֶץ הַזֹּאת, “to give you this land,” אֶת marks הָאָרֶץ הַזֹּאת (“this land”) as the definite direct object of לָתֶת (“to give”).
analysis.morphology: Hebrew direct-object particle with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: הָאָרֶץ הַזֹּאת means “this land.” It is the territory YHWH promises to give Abram, and the feminine singular suffix in לְרִשְׁתָּהּ refers back to it as the land he is to possess.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הָ־ prefixes a common noun in the singular absolute. The noun is tagged for both genders and takes feminine singular agreement here with הַזֹּאת.

draft.change: Add Gen.15.7 as a feminine singular example of the existing this-with-noun sense of זֶה.
draft.definition: The demonstrative follows a definite noun and points out its referent. Here its feminine singular form gives “this land.”
draft.evidence: Gen.15.7 uses the article on both words in הָאָרֶץ הַזֹּאת. The noun names the gift and the demonstrative identifies which land Yahweh means.

analysis.evidence: In לָתֶת לְךָ אֶת הָאָרֶץ הַזֹּאת, “to give you this land,” הַזֹּאת modifies הָאָרֶץ. The feminine singular suffix in לְרִשְׁתָּהּ, “to possess it,” refers back to the same land.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הַ precedes זֹאת, the feminine singular demonstrative of זֶה. The dagesh in ז marks doubling after the article. The demonstrative follows הָאָרֶץ and agrees with it in gender, number and definiteness.
analysis.sense: Points out the particular land Yahweh is giving Abram.

analysis.evidence: In לָתֶת לְךָ אֶת הָאָרֶץ הַזֹּאת, God promises to give Abram “this land.” לְרִשְׁתָּהּ expresses the purpose of the gift, that Abram should take possession of the land.
analysis.morphology: The preposition לְ marks purpose. The Qal infinitive construct takes a third-person feminine singular object suffix referring to הָאָרֶץ, “the land.”
